Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was significantly associated with a current major depressive episode in pregnant women.
Sentence: "In our study, we showed a significant association between current major depressive episode in the antenatal period and vitamin D deficiency (odds ratio [OR]: 0.9; 95%CI 0.9-1.0, p = 0.003)."
Measured as: current major depressive episode in the antenatal period (MINI-Plus diagnosis)
Population: 180 pregnant women up to 24 weeks gestation (130 non-depressed, 50 depressed), Pelotas, Brazil
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D measured by chemiluminescence (vitamin D deficiency); no intervention given
Comparator: Pregnant women without vitamin D deficiency / non-depressed women
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 180
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational vitamin D-depression associations, but Study A's direction is unstated and its population (post-COVID inpatients, PHQ-9 >5 at six months) differs sharply from Study B's pregnant women with diagnosed antenatal major depression.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure","design_or_bias"],"detail":"post-COVID hospital patients at 6 months vs pregnant women up to 24 weeks; PHQ-9 >5 vs MINI-Plus major depressive episode; cohort (n=72) vs case-control (n=180)"}
